claims.text:
The name Finglas is apparently composed by the two elements fing/find "lock of hair" and las "leaf".
The element lock in Leaflock here has the meaning of "hair" since it is a translation of his Sindarin name.
The name obviously refers to his being "Covered with leafy hair".
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, "Nomenclature of The Lord of the Rings" in Wayne G. Hammond and Christina Scull (eds), The Lord of the Rings: A Reader's Companion, p. 760; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Two Towers, "Treebeard"

claims.text: According to Treebeard, Leaflock had become tired, sometimes sleeping through entire seasons (although formerly he used to rouse up in winter), and tree-like with a covering of leafy hair.
